root.label: new and delete
root.note: A new-expression allocates then initializes; a delete-expression destroys then deallocates.

children.label: The new-expression
children.note: Calls an allocation function for raw bytes, then initializes an object in them.

children.label: Sequencing (C++17)
children.note: The allocation function is called before the initializer's arguments are evaluated.

children.label: Constructor throws
children.note: The matching deallocation function frees the storage; no destructor runs.

children.label: std::nothrow
children.note: Allocation failure yields null; a throwing constructor still throws.

children.label: new_handler
children.note: Standard operator new calls the installed handler in a loop before throwing bad_alloc.

children.label: Arrays
children.note: new T[n] calls operator new[] and may request unspecified extra bytes.

children.label: Array cookie
children.note: Itanium stores the count when T has a non-trivial destructor, so delete[] knows n.

children.label: bad_array_new_length
children.note: Thrown for a negative or overflowing size, before any allocation function is called.

children.label: new T[0]
children.note: Valid; returns a distinct non-null pointer that must not be dereferenced.

children.label: Placement forms
children.note: Extra arguments in new (args) T are passed to operator new after the size.

children.label: Non-allocating form
children.note: operator new(size_t, void*) returns its argument and cannot be replaced.

children.label: Placement delete
children.note: Called only when the constructor throws; it must match the extra parameter types.

children.label: Class operator new hides
children.note: A class-specific operator new hides global placement new; write ::new.

children.label: Deallocation functions
children.note: The delete-expression picks one by a fixed preference procedure.

children.label: Sized (C++14)
children.note: Global sized delete is chosen for complete types; for delete[] it needs a non-trivial destructor.

children.label: Aligned (C++17)
children.note: align_val_t overloads are preferred for over-aligned types.

children.label: Destroying delete (C++20)
children.note: Takes T* and destroying_delete_t; the expression skips the destructor.

children.label: Dynamic-type lookup
children.note: With a virtual destructor, operator delete is found in the dynamic type's scope.

children.label: Replacement
children.note: Global definitions of the replaceable functions replace the library's for the whole program.

children.label: Minimal set
children.note: Nothrow, array and sized forms default to calling operator new(size_t) or operator delete(void*).

children.label: Aligned family
children.note: Aligned overloads do not call the unaligned ones and need their own replacement.

children.label: Elision (C++14)
children.note: Calls from new-expressions may be omitted or merged, even when replaced.

children.label: Direct calls
children.note: Calling ::operator new as a function is never elided.

children.label: Undefined mismatches
children.note: Pairing errors the compiler usually cannot detect.

children.label: delete vs delete[]
children.note: Crossing the forms, or with malloc and free, is undefined for every type.

children.label: Non-virtual base
children.note: delete through a base pointer needs a virtual destructor, even if Derived adds nothing.

children.label: delete[] through base
children.note: Undefined whenever the static element type differs from the dynamic one.
